questions.prompt: How many engineers work at your company?
questions.notes: About 2 minutes. Results fill in live as people vote, in order from smallest to largest company. Call out the shape: is this room mostly big companies, or founders preparing for scale? Then: say hi to your neighbors, what does your team build?

questions.prompt: How much of your merged code did an agent write?
questions.notes: About 2 minutes. Guesses are fine. Ask the room: how do you know? Most big teams don't actually measure this. Find someone at either extreme and ask for one sentence on how they got there.

questions.prompt: How locked down are AI tools at your company?
questions.notes: About 2 minutes. This surfaces the big-business reality: procurement, security review, shadow AI. Ask: who made that call, and do people actually follow it? Founders tend to answer anything goes; point out that this is a decision they will eventually have to make.

questions.heading: CHOOSE YOUR FIGHTER

cards.title: ENGINEER
cards.text: You write and review code for a living.

cards.title: FOUNDER
cards.text: You run the company or lead the team.

cards.title: BUILDER
cards.text: You ship with agents, without the engineer title.

questions.notes: About 2 minutes. Each card shows how many people picked that role and their share of the room, live. Call out the mix: it tells everyone who they are talking to. Builders without the engineer title are especially welcome here; say so.

questions.prompt: Which coding agents do you use?
questions.notes: About 2 minutes. People could pick more than one, so call out how many use several agents. Top 8 answers shown, ranked live.

questions.prompt: Which one do you use the most?
questions.notes: About 1 to 2 minutes. Compare with the previous slide: which tools do people try versus actually live in? Ask someone who picked a less common tool why.

questions.prompt: Where do your agents do their work?
options: In the cloud, in the background
questions.notes: About 2 minutes. Editor and terminal use is common; background agents and agents in code review or CI are where big teams start to differ. A good bridge into the open mic.
